items.informal_name: Continuity of $ t^p \left( \frac{1}{t} - \frac{1}{t + x} \right) $ on $ [0, \infty) $ for $ 0 < p < 1 $ and $ t > 0 $
items.type: ∀ {p t : ℝ}, p ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1 → 0 < t → ContinuousOn (p.rpowIntegrand₀₁ t) (Set.Ici 0)
items.informal_description: The function $ f(x) = t^p \left( \frac{1}{t} - \frac{1}{t + x} \right) $ is continuous on the interval $ [0, \infty) $ for all real numbers $ p $ in the open interval $ (0, 1) $ and positive real numbers $ t $. This follows from the constraints $ p \in (0, 1) $ and $ t > 0 $, which ensure the integrand's continuity over the non-negative real numbers.

items.informal_name: Continuity of $ t^p \left( \frac{1}{t} - \frac{1}{t + x} \right) $ on $ (0, \infty) $ for $ p \in (0, 1) $ and $ x \geq 0 $
items.type: ∀ {p x : ℝ}, p ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1 → 0 ≤ x → ContinuousOn (fun x_1 => p.rpowIntegrand₀₁ x_1 x) (Set.Ioi 0)
items.informal_description: The function $ f(t) = t^p \left( \frac{1}{t} - \frac{1}{t + x} \right) $ is continuous on the interval $ (0, \infty) $ for all $ p \in (0, 1) $ and $ x \geq 0 $.

items.informal_name: Continuity of Real Exponentiation Function at Points with Nonzero Base or Positive Exponent
items.type: ∀ (p : ℝ × ℝ), p.1 ≠ 0 ∨ 0 < p.2 → ContinuousAt (fun p => p.1 ^ p.2) p
items.informal_description:
For any real numbers $x$ and $y$, if $x 
eq 0$ or $y > 0$, then the real exponentiation function $f(x, y) = x^y$ is continuous at the point $(x, y)$.

items.informal_name: Continuity of Real Power Function at Points with Positive Exponent
items.type: ∀ (p : ℝ × ℝ), 0 < p.2 → ContinuousAt (fun p => p.1 ^ p.2) p
items.informal_description: The real power function $ (x, y) \mapsto x^y $ is continuous at the point $ (a, b) $ whenever $ b > 0 $.

items.informal_name: Continuity of Real Power Function on Non-negative Reals at Points with $x \neq 0$ or $y > 0$
items.type: ∀ {x : NNReal} {y : ℝ}, x ≠ 0 ∨ 0 < y → ContinuousAt (fun p => p.1 ^ p.2) (x, y)
items.informal_description: The real power function $ f(x, y) = x^y $ defined on the product space $ \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0} \times \mathbb{R} $ is continuous at every point $ (x, y) $ where either $ x \neq 0 $ or $ y > 0 $. The continuity is with respect to the product topology induced by the standard topology on non-negative reals and real numbers.
